summary: offline_repeat's per-workout performance data (repeatFact in internal/cli/offline.go) defaults to a compact summary -- performanceSummaryFields: summaries, average_summaries, duration, effort_zones, splits_data, splits_metrics, summary_available -- rather than the complete raw performance record. A new --full bool flag on offline_repeat opts into the complete record. Any future change to the performance payload shape must keep this allowlist in sync with which fields are genuinely small/summary-like versus which are per-second sample arrays (location_data, metrics, seconds_since_pedaling_start), since the whole point is excluding exactly those large arrays by default.
reason: A round-7 live verification report flagged that offline_repeat's full per-workout performance record (added in offline-repeat-includes-performance.json) risks exceeding the ~60KB MCP result budget for realistic long rides, since the raw record's per-second sample arrays can run into the megabytes. Verified against the real account: location_data alone can be 4.3MB, metrics 522KB, seconds_since_pedaling_start 157KB, while every field in performanceSummaryFields together stays under 15KB even for the largest real record on this account. User chose defaulting to summaries with a --full flag for complete data over other options (e.g. always truncating, or leaving it unbounded).
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. TestOfflineRepeatDefaultsToPerformanceSummaryUnlessFull covers both the default-summary and --full paths against a realistic fixture. Live-verified against the real account with a real workout pair: default JSON output is 1,453 bytes with performance containing only the seven summary fields plus a performance_note pointing to --full; --full on the same pair returns 29,173 bytes including location_data, metrics, seconds_since_pedaling_start, and the rest of the complete record.
